findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - file I/O fused with parsing and unwrap() is a panic surface on missing/unreadable files
findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error; I/O side effects leak into the domain layer
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> with a typed error for I/O and parsing failures; separate the I/O boundary from domain construction

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) - logging (I/O) fused inside the parsing/collection pipeline
findings.failure_mode: Pure parsing logic has a hidden side-effect; output is produced as a byproduct of data loading, breaking functional-core separability and making testing/unittesting unreliable
findings.fix: Remove println from load_packets; move logging to the shell layer after parsing completes

findings.problem: parts[0] - unchecked indexing into a split result that can panic on empty lines or malformed input
findings.failure_mode: An empty line or line without commas panics at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .get(0).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or restructure with split_once to avoid indexing

findings.problem: parts[1] - unchecked indexing into a split result that can panic on lines with fewer than 2 fields
findings.failure_mode: A line with only one comma-separated field panics at runtime instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or restructure with split_once to avoid indexing

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() - parse failure panics on non-numeric value strings
findings.failure_mode: Malformed numeric input aborts the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Replace with .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and propagate through a Result return type

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 - lossy u32-to-u16 cast silently truncates values in range [65536, 4294967295]
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value like 70000 silently truncates to 14440, corrupting domain data with no error or warning
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to fail safely on out-of-range values

findings.problem: Record uses raw primitives (String, u16) with no type-level enforcement of domain invariants
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct a Record with empty names, negative values, or otherwise invalid data without going through a smart constructor or validation
findings.fix: Make Record fields private, add a parse constructor that validates name non-empty and value in-range, and return a typed error on failure

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() - allocates a Vec of all parts instead of using split_once for the two-field grammar
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation for every line; split into Vec when only two fields exist; does not enforce exactly-two-field structure semantically
findings.fix: Replace with let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; to allocate once and enforce the two-field grammar

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures are panics via unwrap()
findings.failure_mode: No way for callers to distinguish file-not-found from malformed-data from overflow; error recovery is impossible
findings.fix: Define enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Invalid, Overflow } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: No pre-allocation budget, no max_items cap, no try_reserve - unbounded growth on large files
findings.failure_mode: A very large input file causes unbounded heap allocation with no cap, potentially OOM-crashing the process
findings.fix: Add a max_items: usize parameter, validate line count or use try_reserve with a domain cap, and reject lines exceeding the cap

findings.problem: load_packets fuses shell (fs::read_to_string, println), parsing (split/parse), and domain construction (Record) into one function
findings.failure_mode: Impossible to unit-test parsing logic in isolation; I/O side effects prevent deterministic testing; violates Data/Calculations/Actions architecture
findings.fix: Split into: parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> (pure), then load_packets(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> (shell that handles I/O and delegates to parse_record)

findings.failure_mode: No measurable proof that the implementation meets any performance, memory, or correctness threshold
findings.fix: Add criterion benchmarks for load_packets with varying input sizes; add allocation profiling evidence
